review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form; encourage a substantially narrowed new submission rather than another ordinary revision in the current round

reviewed_snapshot.source_to_evidence_relation: The evidence commit is one commit ahead of the verified-source commit

remote_execution.review_interpretation: Successful execution and provenance evidence; not journal acceptance or proof of actor superiority

limitations: No machine-formal verification of the interval runtime
No independent retraining of all saved neural policies
No removal of Euler bias from paired payoff comparisons

blocking_findings: The strongest guarantee is architectural and schedule-based rather than created by NBO training.
The actor does not show a robust economic advantage over the schedule.
The fixed-update direct baselines do not isolate the source of the actor's apparent advantage.
The uniform tube certificate cannot distinguish successful from unsuccessful trained actors.
The statistical and numerical evidence for learned improvement is too thin.
The continuous theorem is substantially narrower than the manuscript's general numerical claims.
The economic application is too stylized to carry the paper without a stronger method contribution.
positive_findings: The new continuous-capital theorem was not contradicted and its scalar arithmetic was independently reconstructed.
R10 contains actual multilayer actor-critic and direct-HJB fits in dimensions 10, 20 and 50.
The source, workflow, evidence, raw arrays, weights and tables are strongly bound by manifests and hashes.
Adverse comparisons and scope limitations are retained rather than hidden.
